## Selection probabilities and coefficients

For a fitted `imr` object, `coef(fit)` returns marginal inclusion-probability
matrices. Rows correspond to availability subgroups and columns to features.
`summary(fit)` and `plot_top_features(fit)` rank features by the largest mPIP
attained in a subgroup. This maximum is a ranking score, not the probability
that the feature is included in at least one subgroup.

For an `imr_posterior` object returned by `posterior_draws()`, `coef(post)`
returns regression-coefficient means. `confint(post)` reports coefficient
intervals. See the [uncertainty guide](uncertainty.html) for an executed example.

## Availability patterns

The rightmost bit represents the first platform. With platform order genomic,
proteomic, metabolomic, `011` means genomic plus proteomic and `100` means
metabolomic only. Subgroups with at most `ssize` subjects are excluded from
fitting. Predictions require a matching subgroup retained during training.

Clinical covariates are always included. They are adjustment variables rather
than candidate molecular features. `compare_imr()` describes compatible fits;
it does not automatically select a clinical formula or rank predictive models.

## What `cv_imr()` computes

Version 0.1.3 supplies the historical post-fit fold assessment. It reuses the
full-data selection configurations, latent-response estimates and preprocessing.
The sampler is not rerun within each training fold. The function has no
`cv_method = "refit"` option in this release.

The historical candidate-weighting calculation has additional limitations, so
its scores should not be interpreted as independently validated test accuracy.
An independent refit assessment needs external code to split subjects, refit
preprocessing and selection on training data, and predict the held-out subjects.

## Diagnostics

The fitted object supports the log-posterior score trace, retained theta traces
and selection-indicator traces. For example:

```r
plot(fit, type = "theta_trace", platform = 1, parameter = 1)
plot(fit, type = "selection_trace", platform = 1,
     subgroup = 1, feature = 1)
```

Visual stability is only one diagnostic. Compare longer runs and different
starting states when drawing substantive conclusions. Returned model-average
coefficient rows are pooled and resampled outputs; their row order is not an
MCMC trajectory.

The released selection engine also retains historical differences from the
stated model: its neighbor contribution uses a factor of one for the symmetric
MRF form, and its boundary-flip proposals omit a Hastings correction. Its stored
score retains a positive Gamma-rate term. The documentation examples describe
the fixed release and do not certify those transitions as exact posterior
sampling. Increasing iterations alone does not resolve a target discrepancy.
